# PDF.js for OCR source review

Pinned to the latest stable official release verified on 27 October 2026: [PDF.js 6.4.299](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/releases/tag/v6.4.299), published 3 October 2026. Source: the official npm package [pdfjs-dist 6.4.299](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pdfjs-dist/v/6.4.299), whose `pdfjs-dist-6.4.299.tgz` matches the registry integrity `sha512-AVl138zALtfaAPvADulE0PZThbYzCBS79nL4pOSL/6Sm/4AH5A21BD9VHt97OlCuzJuCpmeZtAtkinisF4Vb1g==` (SHA-256 `86269b40170eb41740ea05ad2102d71d33de4f122b34eb2f478be0ea7779c415`). It is built from the same PDF.js commit (`d0991a0d5`) as the release's [pdfjs-6.4.299-dist.zip](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/releases/download/v6.4.299/pdfjs-6.4.299-dist.zip). `SHA256SUMS` records every vendored upstream file. Upstream files are unmodified.

Included: the minified `build/pdf.min.mjs` and `build/pdf.worker.min.mjs` (placed here), the JBIG2 and JPEG 2000 WASM image decoders from `wasm/`, and their license notices. `src/app/ocr/jobs/job.rs` declares the library, worker and decoders with `asset!`; Topcoat 0.10's MIME detection serves `.mjs` as `application/javascript`. The OCR result passes the decoders' content-hashed URLs to PDF.js's `BinaryDataFactory` with `useWorkerFetch: false`. No CDN, browser build step or remote preview service is used. The decoders load only when a PDF needs them, not when their URLs are rendered.

Omitted: the full upstream viewer, scripting/sandbox/QuickJS support, source maps, locale bundles, JavaScript image-decoder fallbacks, ICC/qcms resources, standard fonts and character maps. This app renders page canvases only and supports browsers with WebAssembly. PDF.js uses its built-in colour conversion, so this is a reading preview rather than a colour-proofing view. Embedded fonts (including the Arabic fixture) render from the PDF. Fonts a PDF does not embed use system fonts, and text in a font that needs one of the omitted character maps (mostly legacy Chinese, Japanese and Korean encodings) is not drawn in the preview. A PDF requiring an unavailable decoder or unsupported feature may fail locally; recognized text, copying and downloads remain available with a source-reselection action.

To update: verify the current stable release on the official release page and the matching `pdfjs-dist` version on npm, replace the included files and notices, regenerate `SHA256SUMS`, then run the OCR review tests in Chromium and WebKit plus the bundled-asset checks. Do not copy a different worker version beside the library.
